messages:
marie: Quick sync — UX problem in Dashboard charts: when panels are narrow the legend and y-axis units squeeze the sparkline and rows get uneven. Thinking of a tiny flyout legend (hover/click) anchored to an icon, or stacking unit chips under a single-line metric. Also debating smoothing UI: a single 'Smoothing' toggle vs a small menu to pick kernel (median vs exp). Outlier treatment: dimming feels like hiding, explicit markers feel better but can clutter. Thoughts?

sam: Flyout legend is nice for touch if activatable by tap. For stacked chips: show tokens `p95 · ms` and keep them tappable to open detail. For smoothing, default to median and offer 'Advanced' menu to choose gaussian. Avoid too many per-chart controls.

alex: Implementation note: median-of-3 is cheap and preserves peaks. Client-side smoothing preferred. Markers: hollow diamond + thin outline works; include a cluster badge `+N` when many overlap. Clicking the cluster expands a lightweight list.

toni: Accessibility checklist: any visual abbreviation must have aria-label with the full phrase, e.g., `aria-label="95th percentile latency (p95) in milliseconds"`. Flyout/popover must be keyboard focusable and use aria-expanded/controls. For markers include aria-describedby with a short SR string: `Anomaly at 2025-11-03 09:00: 12.3 ms (~3x baseline)`. Also provide a 'View anomalies (table)' link for SR users.

preview-bot: Preview: https://staging.redwood.ai/proto/mini-legend-flyout (expires in 24h)

marie: Action items: I will mock the flyout + stacked chips and two smoothing microcopy options: `Smoothing (reduce noise)` and `Smoothing — preserves spikes` (for median). Sam will open the eng ticket for per-chart smoothing default + marker focus. Toni will draft the exact SR strings. Back in ~90m with mocks.
